newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL-LINDROS TO MISS REST OF PRE-SEASON WITH ELBOW INJURY.
newsitem.headline: NHL-LINDROS TO MISS REST OF PRE-SEASON WITH ELBOW INJURY.

text.p: Philadelphia Flyers superstar centre Eric Lindros will miss the rest of the pre-season with an elbow injury but should return for the start of the regular season, the team said Wednesday.

Lindros, 23, had his right elbow drained in Toronto Wednesday to relieve an inflamed bursa sac. He will miss the Flyers' remaining four pre-season games but should be ready for the season opener on Oct. 5 against the Florida Panthers.

"It's not that big a deal," said General Manager Bob Clarke. "He had some water on his elbow and they drained it. If this was a playoff game, he would be playing, obviously. This is the exhibition schedule and he's played enough games already."
Lindros suffered the injury during the World Cup of Hockey earlier this month.
"This is not an uncommon injury to players," Clarke said. "You fall on your elbow, you hit somebody and you get some fluid. That's all it is."

Clarke added: "In the Cup, the bursa sac blew up on him. They took the fluid out and he was OK and he played through it. When he came back, it filled up again. He saw the doctor and they drained it again. He'll be all right in a few days."

Lindros, a finalist last season for the Hart Trophy awarded to the NHL's most valuable player, had 47 goals and a team-leading 115 points as the Flyers posted the best record in the Eastern Conference before they were eliminated in the second round of the playoffs by Florida.
Lindros missed three playoff games in 1994-95 after suffering a cut under his left eye, but won the Hart Trophy.

The big centre was sidelined for 14 games in 1993-94 after suffering a partially torn ligament in his right knee. An unrelated knee injury kept him out of the lineup for 12 games as a rookie in 1992-93.
